# specs/sec-filing-ingestion-roadmap.md

```markdown
# SEC filing ingestion — Roadmap

> For agentic workers: REQUIRED SKILL: derive-roadmap — resume via its
> reconcile step; route each unticked stage per its ROUTING line; never plan
> this document wholesale.

## Outcomes

Source: your partner's words, 2026-11-06. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md, specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md (both Proposed, 2026-10-05).
Choices made: Python 3.14 in the existing uv workspace of four packages.

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | The quarterly and daily index files, ingested into one filing-index table | A | 1 | Small: about 130 quarterly files since 1993 plus one daily file per business day, minutes of downloading at 3 requests/second (SEC full-index and daily-index directories); measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | The individual submissions that the index rows name, downloaded | A | 2 | Large: millions of files, weeks of downloading for the full history at 3 requests/second (index row count times request rate; not yet measured) |
| O3 | 10-K and 8-K filings handled: picked out of the submissions, with their main documents extracted | A | 3 | Unknown until the submissions are on disk |

Tracks: A — SEC filing ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Filing-index table
      Objective: Ingest real quarterly and daily index files into one filing-index table.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing; the package scaffolds only
      Produces: the filing-index table on local storage; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: one table holds the rows of real quarterly and daily index files, with its row count per source file recorded; the findings file records the real run's elapsed time, request count and bytes downloaded
      Leaves out: manifests and provenance (Stage 4); point-in-time reconciliation (Stage 5); full validation suite (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Submission download
      Objective: Download the individual submissions that the filing-index table's rows name.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 1's filing-index table
      Produces: the downloaded submissions on local storage, located from their index rows
      Exit: for a real range of index rows, each named submission is on disk or listed as failed with its reason
      Leaves out: manifests and provenance (Stage 4); full validation suite (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: 10-K and 8-K handling
      Objective: Pick 10-K and 8-K filings out of the downloaded submissions and extract their main documents.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: Stage 2's downloaded submissions; Stage 1's filing-index table
      Produces: extracted main documents for 10-K and 8-K filings, each tied to its submission
      Exit: for the downloaded range, each 10-K and 8-K submission has its main document extracted or is listed as failed with its reason
      Leaves out: manifests and provenance (Stage 4); full validation suite (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Manifests and provenance
      Objective: Record where every row, file and document came from, so work resumes and reprocesses from stored bytes.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3
      Consumes: Stages 1–3 outputs
      Produces: a manifest naming each source file, submission and extracted document with its stored location and content hash
      Exit: O1 — every table row traces to a stored index file and its hash, and rebuilding the table from stored files makes no SEC request; O2 — an interrupted download run resumes without re-fetching completed submissions; O3 — every extracted document traces to its submission
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Point-in-time reconciliation
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes and keep each change as a dated version rather than an overwrite.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: Stage 4's manifest
      Produces: versioned filing-index table with a change record per version
      Exit: O1 — re-reading a changed quarterly index records its additions, changed fields and withdrawals as a new version, and the previous version stays readable
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Full validation suite
      Objective: Cover every stage's behavior with committed fixtures that run in CI without SEC access.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3
      Consumes: Stages 1–5 outputs
      Produces: a CI suite on committed fixtures
      Exit: O1 — CI passes on fixtures for each historical index format in the ingested range, malformed files failing closed; O2 — CI passes on mocked submission downloads including failures and resume; O3 — CI passes on 10-K and 8-K fixtures; no CI run downloads from the SEC
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: Scheduling and deployment
      Objective: Run daily ingestion on a deployed schedule, with catch-up after missed runs.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3
      Consumes: Stages 4–6 outputs
      Produces: a deployed, scheduled daily run
      Exit: O1 — two consecutive scheduled runs ingest the new daily index files, and a run after a deliberately missed one catches up; O2 — those runs download the newly named submissions; O3 — those runs extract the new 10-K and 8-K main documents
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, which writing-plans copies verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-ingestion-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

Retire when every stage is ticked and derive-roadmap §6 re-runs the gap rubric over O1–O3, with evidence per verdict (implementing stage and plan, Deviation notes, deferred_items entries). Each unmet outcome exits as a new stage or as a conscious deferral with a written why.
```

Do you approve this seven-stage partition: the filing-index table as Stage 1, then submissions and 10-K/8-K, then manifests and provenance, point-in-time reconciliation, a full validation suite, and scheduling and deployment as later stages? Or what would you change?
